title: Growing Sending Volume: Follow Delivery Signals, Not a Fixed Calendar
author: Stefan Bogdanescu

content:
Authenticate first

Gmail's sender guidelines set out authentication and DNS requirements. All senders need SPF or DKIM; bulk senders face additional requirements including SPF, DKIM and DMARC. Check the current guidance for your traffic rather than relying on a generic checklist.

Send mail people asked for

Google recommends starting with low volume to engaged recipients and increasing slowly. Recipient complaints and unwanted mail can damage reputation. A warm-up schedule is not a substitute for permission or list hygiene.

Avoid a universal timetable

The appropriate increase depends on volume, sending frequency and recipient feedback. There is no single four-week or eight-week plan that guarantees inbox placement. Monitor delivery results and Postmaster Tools as volume changes.

Know when to slow down

When bounces or deferrals increase, investigate and reduce traffic instead of pushing through a preset target. Keep a record of changes so you can distinguish authentication problems, recipient issues and a volume increase that was too aggressive.

Sources and scope

Configuration and test results determine the behavior of an individual installation. This guide does not certify a live deployment or promise a cost, deliverability or compliance result.
